boardProfile.layout: Block Out Level 144 is a Hard counter board built around purple numbered towers and a seven-bead bottom row with a wrench tool. Border counters tick from `15`/`12`/`20` downward as the towers drain. The two large purple blocks — `6` and `9` — shrink in parallel, and clearing the left stack before the bottom bar hits `17` leaves the wrench tool orphaned with no tower to unlock.
landmarks: Block Out Level 144 is a Hard counter board built around purple numbered towers and a seven-bead bottom row with a wrench tool.
Border counters tick from `15`/`12`/`20` downward as the towers drain.
The two large purple blocks — `6` and `9` — shrink in parallel, and clearing the left stack before the bottom bar hits `17` leaves the wrench tool orphaned with no tower to unlock.

quickTips: Use the purple wrench on the right red bead before breaking the right 9 tower.
Clear the green/red/yellow/green base row on the left before touching the border 15 counter.
Think in chain clears. The best move is the one that sets up the next two moves, not just the quickest current match.

steps.title: Move 1
steps.instruction: Break the top 9 purple block and peel the left numbered stack (6/2/3/1) without touching the wrench bead.

steps.title: Move 2
steps.instruction: Clear the green/red/yellow/green base row on the lower-left flank.

steps.title: Move 3
steps.instruction: Use the purple wrench on the right red bead to unlock the bottom bead row.

steps.title: Move 4
steps.instruction: Clear the right-side blue 4 stack and the adjacent orange/green/red column.

steps.title: Move 5
steps.instruction: Break the remaining large purple 6 and 9 towers once the border counters drop.

steps.title: Move 6
steps.instruction: Spend the left 12/1 rail and the bottom 17 bar on the remaining scraps.

steps.title: Move 7
steps.instruction: Clear the last isolated orange and blue blocks at the base for the board clear.

failurePoints: Clearing the right 9 tower before the wrench bead unlocks, sealing the green/red lower cluster.
Detonating the bead row before the left 6/2/3/1 stack is fully peeled.
